objective: Test whether higher image resolution improves OCT CNV/DRUSEN discrimination from the selected step-20 adapter without overwriting it.

hypothesis.statement: The remaining OCT errors are dominated by DRUSEN/CNV and NORMAL/DRUSEN confusions, so increasing the processed image budget from 65536 to 131072 pixels may preserve more boundary and lesion detail.
hypothesis.result: Not supported. Higher-resolution processing changed the model input distribution and reduced validation performance.

reason: The higher-resolution step-20 initialization validation was 0.826256 macro-F1 and 0.718769 OCT macro-F1, versus 0.873358 and 0.791503 at the verified 65536-pixel input budget.
The best higher-resolution checkpoint reached only 0.832019 macro-F1 and 0.736058 OCT macro-F1, far below the existing step-20 candidate.
Steps 2 and 4 were identical and step 6 fell back to the initialization score, so the run stopped after two validation checks without improvement.
The higher-resolution adapter is not promoted and no frozen-test promotion gate is warranted.
limitations: The 55-row validation set is small and is used only for checkpoint screening.
The frozen OCT test set is not a patient-isolated external validation set.
Higher-resolution inference was not evaluated on the frozen test set because the candidate failed the validation screen.
The stage-3 final and best adapters are experiment outputs, not deployment artifacts.
